whatis.intro: Purchase price variance is the gap between what you paid for an item and its standard price, times the quantity bought. Paying more is unfavorable and paying less is favorable. It measures price alone, with quantity held still. It is how a buyer checks whether a supplier held the agreed price.

cards.title: When the gap is counted
cards.body: Teams differ on when they count it: when the goods arrive or when the invoice posts. Pick one point and hold it, or one month will not compare with the next.
cards.alt: Plus sign, for the point at which the variance is recorded

cards.title: Shorter payment terms slip past it
cards.body: Payment terms. A supplier can hold the $22.00 price and give you fewer days to pay. Your cost of buying rises, and no variance shows it.
cards.alt: Minus sign, for payment terms a price variance does not see

cards.title: Where a distributor starts
cards.body: Start with the lines you buy most. A 1.8% gap on a slow item is small change. The same gap on your busiest line repeats on every delivery.
cards.alt: Light bulb, for starting with the lines bought in the most volume

look.h2: Make the price variance compare like with like
look.intro: The subtraction is exact. The variance is only as honest as three inputs, and each one fails in a familiar way.

steps.title: Overcharges already credited
steps.body: If the supplier has already credited an overcharge, use the corrected price. Otherwise the variance flags a gap that has been settled.

steps.title: The same unit on both sides
steps.body: Check that the standard and the invoice price the same unit. A standard per case against an invoice priced per pound gives a gap that is only arithmetic.

steps.title: Supplier item codes matched to yours
steps.body: A supplier that renumbers an item can make it look new, with no standard at all. Match their item code to your own before you compare.
